units: EUR bn at current prices (the site's 'cur' valuation); 2026 = January-August; value_at_gain = shortfall x Ukraine's net gain per euro (site buy_ukr gain, central); supply_factor = expected / baseline (real, the site's bmul multiplier); positive shortfall = bought more than expected (toward Ukraine), negative = less (toward Russia)
rule: Purchases from Ukraine count both ways. Expected = the buyer's 2021 purchases (the site's base, 2021 held flat) x, product group by group, Ukraine's actual exports to all destinations that year against 2021 (EUR, current prices): the buyer keeps its 2021 share of what Ukraine could actually sell. Buying more than that counts toward Ukraine, buying less toward Russia, at Ukraine's net gain per euro (the site's buy_ukr gain weights), signed and summed 2022 to August 2026 with no floor. Ukraine's own war-caused loss of exports (blocked ports, occupied land, Mariupol, power cuts) lowers the expected level and so counts neither way.

comtrade_ua: UN Comtrade, Ukraine's exports by partner and HS chapter 2021-2024 (reporter 804)
customs_ua: State Customs Service of Ukraine via export.gov.ua and Interfax-Ukraine: exports 2025 and January-August 2026 by product (as in research/2026-10/gaps/net_gain_ukraine.json mix_note)
comext: Eurostat Comext DS-045409, imports from Ukraine of PL, HU, SK, RO, BG by product
site: site/data.json buy_ukr (actual, base, pidx, gain), the site's own valuation
bans_2023: Al Jazeera, 15 Sep 2023: Poland, Hungary, Slovakia keep national bans after the EU measure ends
bans_2026: TVP World, May 2026: Commission presses Poland, Hungary and Slovakia to lift Ukrainian grain bans
romania_licences: Interfax, Oct 2023: Romania approves import licences for Ukrainian wheat, maize, sunflower seed, rapeseed

BGR.name: Bulgaria
BGR.notes: Ban until 15 Sep 2023, then lifted; four-crop purchases stayed above 2021.

BLR.name: Belarus
BLR.notes: Most of its shortfall is Ukraine's own embargo on trade with Belarus, an answer to Belarus hosting the invasion (counted here as a foreseeable answer to its own choice; neutralising it would remove EUR -0.16bn).

CHN.name: China
CHN.notes: Largest charge: its share of Ukraine's grain and oilseeds fell after the Black Sea grain corridor ended (Jul 2023); part of that is shipping risk on the long route, a doubt (route variant: -0.34bn instead of -0.57bn).

HUN.name: Hungary
HUN.notes: National ban on 24 Ukrainian farm products since Sep 2023. Pre-war purchases of the banned crops were near zero, so the ban moves its figure by about 0.

MDA.name: Moldova
MDA.notes: Land neighbour: the route variant measures it against Ukraine's exports to the neighbours only.

POL.name: Poland
POL.notes: National ban on Ukrainian wheat, maize, rapeseed and sunflower seed since 16 Sep 2023 (still in force May 2026). Pre-war it bought almost none of them, so the ban costs little against the no-war level (four crops 2024-2026: about EUR -0.10bn shortfall, -0.008bn at Ukraine's gain); it mostly removes the 2022-2023 surge.

ROU.name: Romania
ROU.notes: Import licences since 13 Oct 2023 for wheat, maize, sunflower seed, rapeseed (processors only); imports of these stayed above their tiny 2021 level.

SVK.name: Slovakia
SVK.notes: National ban on wheat, maize, rapeseed, sunflower seed (and some other farm goods) since Sep 2023; pre-war purchases near zero.
